memory_update.text: WCC belongs in the distributor/integrator bucket for data-center electrical, communications, utility and grid services exposure; evidence is strong for revenue/backlog growth, but bottleneck control is weaker than OEMs because it distributes and integrates rather than manufactures scarce equipment.

NVT maps to electrical connection/protection/enclosure systems for data centers and utilities; treat as a less-obvious component supplier with medium-high thematic relevance pending segment-purity validation.
WIRE should be removed from active public ticker universe; Encore Wire is now part of Prysmian after the July 2, 2024 acquisition and no longer has listed shares.
PRYMY/PRY maps to high-voltage transmission, power grid, North America construction cable and data-center fiber/power cabling; Prysmian also absorbs former Encore Wire exposure.
NEX.PA maps to electrification, PWR-Transmission, PWR-Grid and North American low/medium-voltage cable expansion, with Q1 2026 evidence of data-center activity and €7.9B PWR-Transmission backlog.
SIEGY maps to Smart Infrastructure electrification/electrical products and automation; data-center relationship is current and factual, but conglomerate dilution requires purity adjustment.
SBGSY maps strongly to data-center energy management and power distribution; highest relationship quality in this chunk, but requires valuation-crowding and expectations checks.
ABBNY maps to electrification, automation and data-center/grid demand; relationship is factual but lower-purity than Schneider because ABB spans multiple end markets and product categories.

Layer 2C should add market-pricing checks for WCC, NVT, PRYMY/PRY, NEX.PA, SIEGY, SBGSY and ABBNY: relative performance since AI-power-chain narrative emerged, forward multiples, revisions, short interest and order/backlog expectations.
Need primary filings or transcripts for each ticker to quantify data-center exposure by segment; current evidence often confirms direction but not exact revenue purity or margin contribution.

summary: Candidate chunk maps mostly to the AI/data-center power-chain chokepoint rather than to compute semiconductors directly. Highest relationship quality in this chunk is Schneider Electric, WESCO, Prysmian, nVent, Nexans, Siemens and ABB, because each has current public evidence tying orders, revenue, backlog or strategic focus to data centers, utilities, grid electrification or power distribution. WIRE should be removed as a standalone public ticker because Prysmian completed the Encore Wire acquisition on July 2, 2024 and Encore shares are no longer listed. The key Serenity checks for Layer 2C are purity, backlog durability, pricing power versus pass-through copper exposure, and whether data-center strength is already crowded in valuation.

ticker_relationships.relationship: WESCO is a distributor/integrator across data-center white-space and gray-space infrastructure, including communications infrastructure, electrical distribution, transformers, substations, generators and grid services. This gives it broad exposure to time-to-power and project deployment constraints, but its role is distribution/services rather than proprietary chokepoint manufacturing.
